items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Our cousin Andre Hoffmann and his wife Denise met us

ctx.x: The deal with the policeman and the run-in with the onductor were the only things that made this visit to the States disagreeable.

We arrived in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, the next day. Our cousin Andre Hoffmann and his wife Denise met us and we drove to Sunbury where we spent the night and the next day, visiting the country. Left Sunbury via Harrisburg for New York which was a three hour trip with the train and had the same suite in the Hotel Schluyler that we occupied before going to Cincinnati. George, again, didn't want us to pay anything. We met his mother, Ismay, and we invited her to come to Europe for the summer. Lily offered her to…

We made the rounds of different clubs, were invited to parties and dinners, including one that Herb Flemming prepared for us in his Bronx home. We also caught Ben Webster on his opening night at the Village Vanguard. Ben had a fine trio backing him, but the only musician I can remember was Philly Jo Jones whom I had never met before. Later that night, Tony Scott came in and blew some baritone sax and had a gone jam session with Ben who was playing his can-off that night.
